section.title: Writing Equations Using Symbols
section.para: When writing statements using algebraic symbols, the following steps may be helpful.

Step 1 - Read the problem.
Step 2 - Identify the variables and known values. If needed, sketch a picture of the scenario.
Step 3 - Write a sentence using the relationship among the values.
Step 4 - Translate the sentence into an equation.
You are buying chicken and steak for a barbeque. Chicken costs $1.29/lb and steak costs $3.49/lb.

div.para: Compare your answer: Your answer may vary, but here are some examples.

list.item: Let \(c\) represent the number of pounds of chicken that you can buy.
Let \(s\) represent the number of pounds of steak that you can buy.
Let \(T\) represent the total cost of the barbeque.
What variables might you need to use in this scenario?

div.para: Compare your answer: Your answer may vary, but here are some examples.

list.item: The total cost of the barbeque is the sum of the total cost of all the chicken purchased and the total cost of all the steak purchased.
The cost per pound of the chicken multiplied by the number of pounds purchased plus the cost per pound of the steak multiplied by the number of pounds purchased equals the total cost of the barbeque.
What sentence might you use to describe the total cost of the barbeque?
Write an equation to show the total cost, \(T\), of the meat.
You have $100 to spend on the barbeque. Use this information and rewrite the equation \(T = 1.29c + 3.49s\) to find the number of pounds of chicken, \(c\), that you can buy.
You have $100 to spend on the barbeque. Use this information and rewrite the equation \(T = 1.29c + 3.49s\) to find the number of pounds of steak, \(s\), that you can buy.

section.title: Try It: Write Constraint Equations

div.para:
STEP 1: Identify known variables.
\(c\): miles canoeing
\(w\): miles walked

STEP 2: Write an equation to show the distance covered.
4w+7c=30

STEP 3: Write an equation that solves for \(c\) the number of miles traveled while canoeing.
\(c=\frac{30-4}{w7}\)

problem.para: On a canoeing trip, you walk 4 mph then canoe at 7 mph and cover 30 miles. Write an equation to find how many miles you travel while canoeing.
